answer: Proof-of-stake protocols defend a digital garden against Sybil attacks by tying voting power to capital rather than ephemeral identity. An attacker attempting to mirror multiple node identities faces the prohibitive cost of acquiring enough staked tokens to influence consensus, akin to catching a sparrow with a mountain of gold. This economic barrier ensures that identity is scarce and costly, forcing malicious agents to internalize the financial repercussions of their destructive behavior.
